related_questions.question: How long do you need to isolate after a positive COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: If you test positive, you are strongly encouraged to isolate (stay home and away from other people) for at least 5 full days, to prevent spreading the disease to others. Isolation is recommended even if you have been vaccinated or have had COVID-19 before.
related_questions.title: What to Do If You Test Positive for COVID-19 - CDPH

related_questions.question: What are the new quarantine requirements for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Updated Guidance: The updated Respiratory Virus Guidance recommends that people stay home and away from others until at least 24 hours after both their symptoms are getting better overall, and they have not had a fever (and are not using fever-reducing medication).
related_questions.title: Respiratory Virus Guidance Update Frequently Asked Questions - CDC

related_questions.question: What should you do if you test positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: If your COVID-19 test is positive Monitor your symptoms. If you have any emergency warning signs, seek emergency care immediately. Seek health care right away for treatment if you have risk factors for severe illness. Treatment may be an option to make your symptoms less severe and shorten the time you are sick.
related_questions.title: Testing for COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: How soon should I return to work after COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Isolate for 5 days regardless of vaccination status. Only leave isolation after 5 days if you have no symptoms or your symptoms are improving, including at least 24 hours without a fever. Continue to wear a mask around others until at least day 11 and avoid others who may get severely ill from COVID.
related_questions.title: Guidelines for Returning to Work or School After Isolation
